answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The protection is robust because the trusted grader set is drawn from established agents, which keeps a sudden flood of new keys from capturing majority control. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a orchard as the anchor of the cost.
